This is coming from someone in a country where people only really use guns for hunting, so pardon my ignorance. But what do you actually use your assault weapons for? Are they just to take to a range for fun? or some other reason?

First off, there is no such thing as an "assault weapon". It's a term made up by gun control proponents to scare people into fearing and supporting the ban of guns based on cosmetic features. Josh Sugarmann (a major gun control proponent in the US) openly admitted this when he helped coin the term and then went on to say that the goal was to make uninformed people think that "anything that looks like it could be a machine gun IS a machine gun". There is such a thing as an assault rifle (which refers to any rifle that has a selector to change between semi-auto fire, burst fire, and / or full auto) , but those are heavily restricted in the US and extremely expensive - also, since machine guns became restricted (not banned, just very difficult and expensive to get) in the US in 1934 only two legally owned machine guns have been used in crimes and they both belonged to police officers who chose to misuse their police issued weapon.

As for what they're for? Anything any other rifle is for. Since they literally function exactly like any other semi-automatic rifle and use the same ammunition, you use them for target shooting, hunting (the AR-15 is the most popular hunting rifle in the US currently), or - as the Second Amendment to the US Constitution was primarily intended - if the need ever arises, you use them against the government troops who violate your rights. The features that make a rifle an "assault weapon" (read: scary looking) are purely cosmetic and usually involve safety / comfort features. For instance, a barrel shroud protects you from burning your hand, a pistol grip makes it easier to hold the rifle correctly and thus easier to aim, an adjustable stock makes it so you can adjust it for the length of your arms, a flash hider helps keep you from getting a flash of light in your eyes and being momentarily "dazed", etc. None of these features affects the functionality of the rifle in any way.

Here's a great example of how asinine the idea of "assault weapons" is: The Ruger Mini-14.
